message.content:
Here’s a list of the long weekends in Canada for 2023. A long weekend is defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, giving you a three‑day weekend (or sometimes a four‑day weekend if the holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday and is observed on a weekday).

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1–2** | New Year’s Day | Observed on Monday, Jan 2 (holiday falls on Sunday) |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Ontario, PEI, NB, BC) | Observed on Monday, Feb 20 |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday | Observed on Friday, Apr 7 |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | Observed on Monday, May 22 |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day | Observed on Monday, Jul 3 (holiday falls on Saturday) |
| **Aug 5–7** | Civic Holiday (varies by province) | Observed on Monday, Aug 7 |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | Observed on Monday, Sep 4 |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | Observed on Monday, Oct 9 |
| **Nov 9–11** | Remembrance Day | Observed on Monday, Nov 11 |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas Day | Observed on Monday, Dec 25 |
| **Dec 24–26** | Boxing Day | Observed on Tuesday, Dec 26 (holiday falls on Tuesday, giving a four‑day weekend from Thu 24 to Sat 26) |

These are the official federal holidays that create long weekends in Canada for 2023. Some provinces have additional holidays that may also create long weekends, but the above list covers the nationwide ones.
